policy: Persistent append-only, novelty/evidence-specific, nonduplicated; 1/3 does NOT mean original science, N2 requires independent strong confirmation

findings.claim: At small integer label budgets, many nominally different continuous allocation mixtures map to identical three-stratum allocation vectors; 81-90% redundant across observed sources on the preselected grid.
findings.evidence: Post-exposure R1 repaired experiments, exact enumeration
findings.falsifier: Alternative integer budgets and constraints with more distinct treatment vectors
findings.possible_composition: Optimize unique implementable policies and protect against auxiliary-objective misspecification

findings.claim: Exact optimal integer allocation on an imperfect auxiliary variance proxy can worsen true outcome variance relative to a less exact Hamilton approximation; five of six observed populations in one study.
findings.evidence: Post-exposure R1 repaired finite population design variance comparisons
adversarial_limits: proxy selection and scoring not field validated
findings.falsifier: Proxy calibrated strongly predicts within-stratum target variance, reversing outcome
findings.possible_composition: Policy equivalence classes under bounded auxiliary uncertainty and fixed integer budgets

findings.claim: In six observed finite populations, a six-label pilot can improve allocation relative to a raw noisy pilot after 70% auxiliary-variance shrinkage, yet fails to improve full-budget population risk variance against a competent no-pilot comparator; a separate post-hoc audit reusing pilot labels still showed higher MSE under tested budgets.
findings.evidence: Three prospectively specified six-source AB blocks plus a POSTSELECTED competent pilot-reuse audit with 500 finite-population random trials per source and budget; G larger budgets on same data, not independent replication.
adversarial_limits: original pilot method excludes pilot labels from final estimate, a weak design
post-run reuse test is exploratory, not new field data
strong Bayesian and multi-wave design literature exists
no independent external replication or publication-level novelty
findings.falsifier: A budget-parity, fully efficient multi-wave field implementation beats competent one-wave controls in a preregistered independent dataset under measured label costs
findings.possible_composition: Integer policy quotient + proxy-target calibration + value-of-information under observable real label prices
findings.novelty_assessed: NO 2/3; known category of design and acquisition cost

findings.claim: When pilot labels are acquired before an induced change in the outcome, reusing them as if contemporaneous can increase bias, but paying to refresh them may worsen the mean squared error at fixed total label-action budget.
findings.evidence: B10 finite-population MC: stale-pilot HT greater absolute bias in 5/5 exploratory sources E and 4/5 G while lower MSE than stage2-only; B11 buying another six labels to refresh stale pilot led to worse MSE in 5/5 E and G. B=30 and 48, same historical data, outcome shifts constructed post-pilot. R1 no-leakage fixed transformation selected after observing earlier invalid results.
adversarial_limits: All label changes are artificially constructed; no naturally observed temporal drift
Public historical datasets reused, no outside prospective deployment
R1 repair after exposure, not blind confirmation
Conditional unbiasedness and missing-label methods predate study
The cost tradeoff overlaps COST-PILOT-03, but temporal validity is a distinct operational failure mode
No field measurements of real labels and price
No claim of a new statistical theorem
findings.possible_composition: Explicit time-indexed estimand and label-age-aware acquisition with equivalence-class compression, honest proxy-target gap and actual remeasurement costs
findings.falsifier: A preregistered real-time independent stream finds refreshed pilot labels improve net risk estimation enough to offset measured reacquisition cost, or there is no temporal bias in production outcome under detected drift.
findings.novelty_assessed: NOT 2/3; classical sequential survey principles cover broad effect

pending_historical_audit: Many older LARP reports predate explicit 1/3 grading. Do not infer that no other 1/3 exist; enumerate and assess before adding to historical total.
